question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam was a great man with a high level of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. intellect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Intellect" means the power of the mind to think, reason and understand logically. (बुद्धि / मेधा) The sentence praises Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, a scientist and the 11th President of India, so "a high level of intellect" is the only meaningful and collocationally correct filler.

◦ Correct: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam was a great man with a high level of intellect.

• The fixed collocation is "a high level of + abstract quality" — a high level of intellect / confidence / commitment / skill.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "intelligent humour" — "intelligent" is an adjective used for a person, not for the quality of humour in this frame; the phrase does not fit "a great man with a high level of".

• Option 2 "wise boredom" is a contradiction in terms — boredom (ऊब) is never praised.

• Option 4 "clever fatigue" is meaningless; fatigue (थकान) cannot be "clever".

NOTE

• Word family: intellect (noun), intellectual (adjective/noun), intelligence (the ability to acquire and apply knowledge), intelligible (able to be understood).

• Similar SSC collocations: "a man of letters", "a man of few words", "a person of high calibre".

question:
The following sentence contains some errors. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

The forses that genarate conditions conduciive to crime and riiots are stronger in urban communities than in rurral areas.
option_1: The forsec that genarate conditions conduciive to crime and riots are stronger in urban communities than in rurall areas.
option_2: The forces that genereta conditions conducieve to crime and riotts are stronger in urban communities than in rural areas.
option_3: The forces that generate conditions conducive to crime and riots are stronger in urban communities than in rural areas.
option_4: The forces that genarete conditions conduciive to crime and riots are stronger in urban communities than in ruraal areas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The forces that generate conditions conducive to crime and riots are stronger in urban communities than in rural areas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a spelling-correction item. The given sentence misspells five words. Only Option 3 spells every one of them correctly:

◦ "forses" → "forces" (शक्तियाँ / बल)

◦ "genarate" → "generate" (उत्पन्न करना)

◦ "conduciive" → "conducive" (अनुकूल; conducive to something)

◦ "riiots" → "riots" (दंगे)

◦ "rurral" → "rural" (ग्रामीण)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 still keeps the wrong forms "forsec", "genarate", "conduciive" and "rurall".

• Option 2 still keeps "genereta", "conducieve" and "riotts".

• Option 4 still keeps "genarete", "conduciive" and "ruraal".

NOTE

• Spelling keys: FOR + CES, GEN + ER + ATE, CON + DU + CIVE, RI + OTS, RU + RAL.

• "Conducive" is always followed by the preposition "to" — "an atmosphere conducive to study".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I found my teacher’s points casual and informal in the group discussion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. free and easy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "free and easy" means relaxed, casual and informal; not bound by strict rules. (सहज और अनौपचारिक) It is the exact idiomatic substitute for the underlined segment "casual and informal".

◦ Correct: I found my teacher's points free and easy in the group discussion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "flesh and blood" means one's own family/relatives, or human nature (अपना सगा-संबंधी).

• Option 3 "foot the bill" means to pay the bill/expenses (खर्च उठाना).

• Option 4 "fair and square" means honestly and straightforwardly (ईमानदारी से).

NOTE

• Note the difference: "free and easy" (relaxed manner) vs "easy come, easy go" (money gained easily is lost easily).

• Other binomial idioms for SSC: "rough and ready", "part and parcel", "null and void", "by and large", "safe and sound".

question:
Select the word which means the same as the group of words given.

One who is all powerful.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Omnipotent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Omnipotent" means one who is all-powerful; having unlimited power. (सर्वशक्तिमान) The Latin roots are "omni-" (all) + "potens" (powerful).

◦ Example: Believers hold that God is omnipotent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Omnipresent" — present everywhere at the same time (सर्वव्यापी).

• Option 3 "Optimist" — a person who looks at the bright side of things (आशावादी).

• Option 4 "Omniscient" — one who knows everything (सर्वज्ञ).

NOTE

• The "omni-" family is a favourite of SSC: omnipotent (all-powerful), omnipresent (present everywhere), omniscient (all-knowing), omnivorous (eating both plants and flesh), omnibus (a volume containing several works).

• Related pairs: optimist × pessimist; theist × atheist.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Ramesh is owning a beautiful house in Noida.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. owns.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Own" is a stative verb (a verb of possession). Stative verbs are not used in continuous (progressive) tenses, so "is owning" is wrong; the simple present "owns" must be used.

◦ Correct: Ramesh owns a beautiful house in Noida.

• The subject "Ramesh" is third person singular, so the verb takes "-s" — owns.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "did owned" is wrong — after "did" the base form (V1) is used ("did own"), and even that is emphatic, not required here.

• Option 3 "has owning" is not a valid structure ("has owned" would be the present perfect).

• Option 4 "was owned" is a passive form and reverses the intended meaning (the house is owned, not Ramesh).

NOTE

• Common stative verbs never used in the continuous form: own, possess, belong, have (possess), know, understand, believe, like, love, hate, want, need, seem, contain, consist, resemble.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

When Nisha will have finished her task?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. When Nisha will.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In an interrogative sentence the auxiliary/helping verb must come BEFORE the subject. The correct order after the question word "When" is "will Nisha", not "Nisha will".

◦ Correct: When will Nisha have finished her task?

• Structure of a WH-question: WH-word + auxiliary + subject + main verb + object.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "have" and "finished" together form the future perfect "will have finished", which is correct.

• "her task" is the correct object.

NOTE

• Compare: "Where is he going?" (correct) / "Where he is going?" (wrong).

• Inversion is dropped only in indirect/reported questions: "Tell me when Nisha will have finished her task." (no question mark, no inversion).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He push the bushes aside and went a little farther.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. pushed the bushes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The second verb of the sentence, "went", is in the simple past tense. By the rule of parallelism of tense, the first verb must also be in the simple past — "pushed".

◦ Correct: He pushed the bushes aside and went a little farther.

• The object "the bushes" (plural, definite) is retained unchanged; only the verb form needs correction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "pushed with bush" changes the meaning and drops the article.

• Option 2 "pushing the bush" is a participle and leaves the clause without a finite verb.

• Option 3 "pushes in bush" is simple present and clashes with "went".

NOTE

• When two actions joined by "and" happen in the same time frame, both verbs must be in the same tense: "He opened the door and walked in."

• Note also "farther" (physical distance) vs "further" (extent/degree).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Copying someone else’s work and trying to submit it as your own
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Plagiarism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Plagiarism" means the act of copying another person's work, ideas or words and passing them off as one's own. (साहित्यिक चोरी)

◦ Example: The student's thesis was rejected for plagiarism.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Polygamy" — the practice of having more than one spouse at a time (बहुविवाह).

• Option 3 "Preamble" — an introductory statement, e.g., the Preamble to the Constitution (प्रस्तावना).

• Option 4 "Extempore" — a speech delivered without previous preparation (तत्काल / बिना तैयारी).

NOTE

• Related words: plagiarise (verb), plagiarist (the person).

• Other marriage-related one-word substitutes: monogamy (one spouse), bigamy (two spouses), polyandry (many husbands), polygyny (many wives), celibacy (abstaining from marriage).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Beauty of it
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Good points.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "the beauty of it" is used to point out the best or most advantageous feature of something — its good points. (सबसे अच्छी बात यह है कि …)

◦ Example: The scheme is cheap, and the beauty of it is that anyone can join.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Make things worse" corresponds to the idiom "add fuel to the fire" / "to make matters worse".

• Option 2 "Cause for dispute" corresponds to "bone of contention" / "apple of discord".

• Option 3 "Quite ordinary" corresponds to "run of the mill" / "nothing to write home about".

NOTE

• Related expressions: "beauty is in the eye of the beholder" (beauty is a matter of personal taste), "beauty is only skin deep" (outer looks are not what really matter).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

The girl was manacled and locked in the room.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. fettered.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Manacled" means handcuffed; bound with chains or shackles. (हथकड़ी लगाना / बेड़ियों में जकड़ना) Its closest synonym is "fettered", which means chained or shackled (especially by the feet), and hence restrained.

◦ Example: The prisoner was manacled/fettered before being taken to court.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "unfastened" (untied/loosened) and Option 2 "liberated" (set free) are antonyms.

• Option 4 "unbinded" is not a word at all; the correct form would be "unbound".

NOTE

• Synonyms of manacled: fettered, shackled, handcuffed, chained, bound, restrained.

• Antonyms: freed, released, liberated, unshackled, unfettered.

• Noun forms: a manacle is a handcuff; a fetter is a leg-iron. Figuratively, "the fetters of tradition" means its restrictions.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

Addiction of drugs proved detrimental for his health.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Beneficial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Detrimental" means harmful; causing damage or injury. (हानिकारक) Its exact antonym is "beneficial", meaning helpful or advantageous. (लाभदायक)

◦ Example: Smoking is detrimental to health, whereas exercise is beneficial.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Impartial" — unbiased, fair (निष्पक्ष).

• Option 2 "Potential" — possible/latent capacity (संभावित).

• Option 4 "Differential" — relating to a difference (विभेदक).

These three are unrelated to "harmful" and are only sound-alike distractors.

NOTE

• Synonyms of detrimental: harmful, injurious, damaging, deleterious, adverse, prejudicial.

• Antonyms: beneficial, advantageous, helpful, favourable, salutary.

• Usage: "detrimental to health" is the standard preposition.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Plunge
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Dive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Plunge" means to jump or dive suddenly into water; to fall/throw oneself steeply downward. (गोता लगाना / अचानक गिरना) Its closest synonym is "dive".

◦ Example: He plunged/dived into the river to save the child.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Transgress" — to break a law or moral rule (उल्लंघन करना).

• Option 3 "Rush" — to move hurriedly; it conveys speed but not the downward/into-water sense.

• Option 4 "Fly" — to move through the air, the opposite direction of a plunge.

NOTE

• Synonyms of plunge: dive, submerge, immerse, nosedive, plummet, descend.

• Antonyms: rise, ascend, soar, emerge.

• "Plunge" is also used figuratively: "share prices plunged", "the country was plunged into crisis", "take the plunge" (to decide to do something risky at last).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Tomatos.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tomatos" is misspelt. The correct plural of "tomato" is "tomatoes" (टमाटर). Nouns ending in a consonant + o normally take "-es" in the plural.

◦ Correct: potato → potatoes, tomato → tomatoes, hero → heroes, mango → mangoes, echo → echoes, volcano → volcanoes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Weather" (the state of the atmosphere — मौसम), "Vehicle" (a means of transport — वाहन) and "Professor" (a senior university teacher — प्राध्यापक) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words ending in a vowel + o simply add "-s": radio → radios, studio → studios, bamboo → bamboos, zoo → zoos.

• Musical terms also take only "-s": piano → pianos, photo → photos, solo → solos.

• Do not confuse the homophones weather (मौसम), whether (conjunction — क्या/चाहे) and wether (a castrated ram).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.

I used a variety of sources to find the more cheap flight.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. cheapest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "More cheap" is grammatically wrong. "Cheap" is a one-syllable adjective, so its degrees are formed with "-er / -est", never with "more/most":

◦ cheap (positive) – cheaper (comparative) – cheapest (superlative).

• Here the speaker searched "a variety of sources", i.e., compared more than two options, and the definite article "the" precedes the blank. "the + superlative" is the required structure, so "the cheapest flight" is correct.

◦ Correct: I used a variety of sources to find the cheapest flight.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because the segment definitely needs rectification.

• Option 2 "cheaper" is the comparative and would need a "than" clause or a comparison between exactly two flights; it does not suit "the ... flight" after searching many sources.

• Option 4 "cheap" (positive degree) cannot follow "the" in this comparison-based sentence.

NOTE

• Degree rules: one-syllable and many two-syllable adjectives take -er/-est (tall–taller–tallest, cheap–cheaper–cheapest); longer adjectives take more/most (beautiful – more beautiful – most beautiful).

• A double comparative/superlative such as "more cheaper" or "most cheapest" is always incorrect.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

All the members of my family are planning to visit Jammu and Kashmir this Novembur.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Novembur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Novembur" is misspelt. The correct spelling of the eleventh month is "November" — the last syllable is "-ber", not "-bur". (नवंबर)

◦ Correct: All the members of my family are planning to visit Jammu and Kashmir this November.

• Spelling key: NO + VEM + BER.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Planning" (double "n" because "plan" ends in a single vowel + single consonant and the stress is on the last syllable), "Visit" and "Members" are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• The four "-ber" months: September, October, November, December. Names of months always begin with a capital letter.

• Doubling rule: plan → planning, stop → stopping, begin → beginning; but visit → visiting, open → opening (stress not on the last syllable).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Ravi will go to the England.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the England.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The definite article "the" is NOT used before the names of most countries, and England is one of them. So "the England" is wrong; it must simply be "England".

◦ Correct: Ravi will go to England.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Ravi" (proper noun subject), "will" (future auxiliary) and "go to" (verb + preposition of direction) are all correct.

NOTE

• "The" is used with country names that are plural, or that contain words like Republic/Kingdom/States: the Netherlands, the Philippines, the USA, the UK, the UAE, the Maldives.

• "The" is also used with rivers (the Ganga), oceans (the Pacific), mountain ranges (the Himalayas), deserts (the Thar) and holy books (the Ramayana), but NOT with single mountains (Mount Everest) or single islands.

question:
Select the most appropriate response in the given situation of the eve of a battle to fill in the blank.

The commander: “Honourable Emperor, all the troops have lined up for the battle and are awaiting your orders.” Emperor Chandragupta Maurya: “______________________.”
option_2: You should learn how to talk to an emperor.
option_4: We are ready for the pilgrimage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. We will march at dawn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a situation-based / conversational response question. The commander reports that the troops have lined up for battle and await orders; therefore the Emperor's reply must be an order relating to the battle.

• "We will march at dawn" is a clear, appropriate military command — the army will advance at daybreak. (हम भोर में कूच करेंगे)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "You should learn how to talk to an emperor" is a rude rebuke; the commander has already addressed him respectfully as "Honourable Emperor", so there is nothing to object to.

• Option 3 "We will be playing cards" is frivolous and totally out of place on the eve of a battle.

• Option 4 "We are ready for the pilgrimage" is irrelevant — a pilgrimage (तीर्थयात्रा) has nothing to do with a battle.

NOTE

• In such items, always ask: (i) who is speaking, (ii) to whom, and (iii) what tone the situation demands (formal, polite, commanding, apologetic).

• Static link: Chandragupta Maurya (c. 322–298 BCE) founded the Mauryan Empire with the guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya), the author of the Arthashastra.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

We prefer going to movies once in a blue moon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Very rarely.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "once in a blue moon" means very rarely; hardly ever. (कभी-कभार / बहुत कम)

◦ Example: He visits his home town once in a blue moon.

• The phrase comes from the astronomical "blue moon" — the second full moon in a single calendar month, which is an uncommon event.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "Very often" is the exact opposite of the idiom's meaning.

• Option 2 "Very amazingly" and Option 3 "Very diligently" (with great care and effort) have no connection with frequency.

NOTE

• Idioms of rarity: "once in a blue moon", "few and far between", "at long intervals".

• Idioms of frequency: "every now and then", "time and again", "day in and day out", "more often than not".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

My father told me / that in his childhood / he was walking / to school every day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. he was walking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "every day" shows a repeated, habitual action in the past. A habit in the past is expressed by the simple past ("walked") or by "used to walk", never by the past continuous.

◦ Correct: My father told me that in his childhood he walked (or used to walk) to school every day.

• The past continuous "was walking" describes an action in progress at a particular past moment, which contradicts "every day".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "My father told me" is correct (told + indirect object).

• "that in his childhood" correctly introduces the reported clause with an adverbial of time.

• "to school every day" is correct — "school" takes no article when it refers to the institution/activity.

NOTE

• Reported speech: when the reporting verb is in the past ("told"), the reported verb also shifts to the past — present simple → past simple.

• "Used to + V1" is the classic marker of a discontinued past habit: "He used to smoke, but he doesn't now."

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.

Today’s question paper felt like a cakewalk.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Very easy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a cakewalk" (also "a piece of cake") means something very easy to do; an effortless task. (बहुत आसान काम)

◦ Correct sense: Today's question paper felt very easy.

• The expression comes from a 19th-century dance contest in which a cake was the prize — the winner simply had to "walk" gracefully.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Very sweet" and 2 "Very tasty" are literal traps based on the word "cake"; idioms are never taken literally.

• Option 4 "Very difficult" is the opposite meaning.

NOTE

• Idioms meaning "easy": a piece of cake, a cakewalk, child's play, as easy as ABC, a walk in the park, plain sailing.

• Idioms meaning "difficult": a hard nut to crack, an uphill task, a tall order, no bed of roses.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Modern football (1)________in Britain in the 19th century. Since before medieval times, ‘folk football’ games had been played in towns and villages according to local customs and with a (2)_______of rules. Industrialisation and (3)________, which reduced the amount of leisure time and space available to the working class, combined with a history of legal prohibitions against particularly (4)________ and destructive forms of folk football to undermine the game’s status from the early 19th century onward. However, football was taken up as a winter game between residence houses at public (independent) schools such as Winchester, Charterhouse and Eton. Each school had its own rules; some allowed limited handling of the ball and others did not. The (5)_________in rules made it difficult for public schoolboys entering university to continue playing except with former schoolmates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. originated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Originate" means to begin; to come into existence; to have its source in a place. (उत्पन्न होना / आरंभ होना) The passage traces the beginning of modern football in Britain in the 19th century.

◦ Correct: Modern football originated in Britain in the 19th century.

• The whole paragraph then describes how the game developed from folk football — a beginning, not an end.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "terminated" means ended/stopped — the opposite of what the passage says.

• Option 2 "culminated" means reached its highest point/climax, and normally takes "in" a final result, not a starting point.

• Option 4 "fragmented" means broke into pieces, which does not fit "in Britain in the 19th century".

NOTE

• Synonyms of originate: begin, arise, stem from, emanate, spring up, commence.

• Word family: origin (noun), original (adjective), originality (noun), originator (one who starts something).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Modern football (1)________in Britain in the 19th century. Since before medieval times, ‘folk football’ games had been played in towns and villages according to local customs and with a (2)_______of rules. Industrialisation and (3)________, which reduced the amount of leisure time and space available to the working class, combined with a history of legal prohibitions against particularly (4)________ and destructive forms of folk football to undermine the game’s status from the early 19th century onward. However, football was taken up as a winter game between residence houses at public (independent) schools such as Winchester, Charterhouse and Eton. Each school had its own rules; some allowed limited handling of the ball and others did not. The (5)_________in rules made it difficult for public schoolboys entering university to continue playing except with former schoolmates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. minimum.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage says folk football was played "according to local customs" — that is, informally, with hardly any codified regulations. Hence it was played "with a minimum of rules", i.e., with very few rules. (न्यूनतम नियमों के साथ)

◦ Correct: ... played in towns and villages according to local customs and with a minimum of rules.

• "A minimum of + noun" is a standard English structure meaning "as little as possible / very little".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "maximum" contradicts the informal, customary nature of folk football.

• Option 1 "optimum" (the most favourable amount) does not suit a game that had no fixed code at all.

• Option 2 "variance" is the answer to blank no. 5, where the passage explicitly contrasts different school rules; in blank 2 the point is the scarcity, not the difference, of rules.

NOTE

• Related expressions: "a minimum of fuss", "keep costs to a minimum", "the bare minimum".

• Antonym pair for SSC: minimum (least) × maximum (greatest); minimise × maximise.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Modern football (1)________in Britain in the 19th century. Since before medieval times, ‘folk football’ games had been played in towns and villages according to local customs and with a (2)_______of rules. Industrialisation and (3)________, which reduced the amount of leisure time and space available to the working class, combined with a history of legal prohibitions against particularly (4)________ and destructive forms of folk football to undermine the game’s status from the early 19th century onward. However, football was taken up as a winter game between residence houses at public (independent) schools such as Winchester, Charterhouse and Eton. Each school had its own rules; some allowed limited handling of the ball and others did not. The (5)_________in rules made it difficult for public schoolboys entering university to continue playing except with former schoolmates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. urbanisation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Urbanisation" means the growth of towns and cities and the movement of people from villages into them. (शहरीकरण) The passage says the process "reduced the amount of leisure time and space available to the working class" — exactly what industrialisation and urbanisation together did in 19th-century Britain.

◦ Correct: Industrialisation and urbanisation, which reduced the amount of leisure time and space available to the working class ...

• "Industrialisation and urbanisation" is a standard collocation in social history.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "normalisation" (making something normal/standard) and Option 3 "standardisation" (making things uniform) would not reduce space for the working class.

• Option 4 "implementation" (putting a plan into effect) is incomplete without an object and makes no sense here.

NOTE

• Static link: The Industrial Revolution in Britain (c. 1760–1840) caused mass migration to factory towns, overcrowding and the loss of open commons where folk football had been played.

• Related terms: urban (of a city), rural (of the countryside), suburban (of the outskirts), metropolis (a very large city).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Modern football (1)________in Britain in the 19th century. Since before medieval times, ‘folk football’ games had been played in towns and villages according to local customs and with a (2)_______of rules. Industrialisation and (3)________, which reduced the amount of leisure time and space available to the working class, combined with a history of legal prohibitions against particularly (4)________ and destructive forms of folk football to undermine the game’s status from the early 19th century onward. However, football was taken up as a winter game between residence houses at public (independent) schools such as Winchester, Charterhouse and Eton. Each school had its own rules; some allowed limited handling of the ball and others did not. The (5)_________in rules made it difficult for public schoolboys entering university to continue playing except with former schoolmates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. violent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is joined by "and" to the adjective "destructive", so the missing word must also be an adjective with a similar negative sense. "Violent" (using or involving physical force intended to hurt — हिंसक) pairs naturally with "destructive".

◦ Correct: ... legal prohibitions against particularly violent and destructive forms of folk football ...

• It also explains why laws prohibited those forms of the game.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "traces" and 2 "undercurrents" are nouns and cannot stand parallel to the adjective "destructive".

• Option 3 "calm" is an adjective but has the opposite sense — nobody bans a game for being calm.

NOTE

• Rule of parallelism: words joined by "and" must belong to the same grammatical class (adjective + adjective, noun + noun, verb + verb).

• Collocations: "violent and destructive", "swift and decisive", "rough and tumble".

• Historical note: medieval folk football was so rough that English monarchs, including Edward II (1314), issued proclamations banning it.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Modern football (1)________in Britain in the 19th century. Since before medieval times, ‘folk football’ games had been played in towns and villages according to local customs and with a (2)_______of rules. Industrialisation and (3)________, which reduced the amount of leisure time and space available to the working class, combined with a history of legal prohibitions against particularly (4)________ and destructive forms of folk football to undermine the game’s status from the early 19th century onward. However, football was taken up as a winter game between residence houses at public (independent) schools such as Winchester, Charterhouse and Eton. Each school had its own rules; some allowed limited handling of the ball and others did not. The (5)_________in rules made it difficult for public schoolboys entering university to continue playing except with former schoolmates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. variance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Variance" means difference or divergence between things. (भिन्नता / मतभेद) The previous sentence states that "Each school had its own rules; some allowed limited handling of the ball and others did not" — that is, the rules differed. Hence "the variance in rules" made joint play difficult.

◦ Correct: The variance in rules made it difficult for public schoolboys entering university to continue playing except with former schoolmates.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "grouse" means a complaint/to grumble (and also a game bird) — it does not explain the difficulty.

• Option 2 "grunt" is a low guttural sound made by a person or a pig.

• Option 4 "control" would suggest regulation, but uniform control would have made joint play easier, not harder.

NOTE

• Word family: vary (verb), various/variable (adjectives), variety, variation, variance (nouns).

• Useful phrase: "at variance with" = in disagreement or conflict with. "His statement is at variance with the facts."

• Static link: The differing school codes led to the founding of The Football Association (FA) in 1863, which finally standardised the laws of the game.

question: Identify the vector quantity among these listed physical quantities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gravitational Intensity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction and follows the laws of vector addition. Gravitational intensity (also called gravitational field strength, defined as force per unit mass, g = F/m) has a definite direction — towards the centre of the attracting body — so it is a vector. (गुरुत्वीय तीव्रता — सदिश राशि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Energy, Mass and Density are scalar quantities — they are fully described by magnitude alone and have no direction.

• Other common scalars: distance, speed, time, temperature, work, power, volume, pressure, electric charge, electric potential.

• Other common vectors: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, weight, momentum, impulse, torque, electric field, magnetic field.

NOTE

• Unit of gravitational intensity: N/kg (equivalent to m/s²). At the Earth's surface its value is about 9.8 N/kg.

• Remember: weight (mg) is a vector, but mass is a scalar; velocity is a vector, but speed is a scalar.

question: ‘The Palace of Illusions’, a rendition of the Hindu epic ‘Mahabharata’, was written by which of the following novelists?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Palace of Illusions" (2008) was written by the Indian-American author Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni. It retells the Mahabharata from the point of view of Draupadi (Panchaali). (द पैलेस ऑफ इल्यूजन्स — चित्रा बनर्जी दिवाकरुनी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Her other well-known works include The Mistress of Spices, Sister of My Heart, The Forest of Enchantments (the Ramayana told by Sita) and The Last Queen (on Rani Jindan).

• Pratibha Ray is the Odia writer of "Yajnaseni", another acclaimed Draupadi-centred novel; she won the Jnanpith Award (2011).

• Indu Sundaresan wrote "The Twentieth Wife" (on Nur Jahan) and Devi Yesodharan wrote "Empire".

NOTE

• Other modern retellings of the epics: The Palace of Illusions (Divakaruni), The Great Indian Novel (Shashi Tharoor), Jaya (Devdutt Pattanaik), Ajaya and Asura (Anand Neelakantan).

question: G Krishnakumar was appointed chairman of which of the following in 2023?
option_1: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• G Krishnakumar was appointed Chairman and Managing Director of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) in 2023. (भारत पेट्रोलियम कॉर्पोरेशन लिमिटेड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• BPCL is a Maharatna public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, headquartered in Mumbai. It operates refineries at Mumbai, Kochi and Bina.

• ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation) is India's largest crude oil and natural gas producer, headquartered in New Delhi.

• IOCL (Indian Oil Corporation Ltd) is the country's largest oil refining and marketing company, headquartered in New Delhi.

• HPCL (Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd) is headquartered in Mumbai and is a subsidiary of ONGC.

NOTE

• India's Maharatna oil PSUs include IOCL, ONGC, BPCL, HPCL and GAIL. The Maharatna status gives them greater autonomy in investment decisions.

question: ______________ was the first Indian woman to write an autobiography and also the first to do so in Bengali in her book titled ‘Aamar Jiban’, which was published in 1876.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rassundari Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rassundari Devi (1809–1899) was the first Indian woman to write a full-length autobiography, and the first to do so in Bengali. Her book "Aamar Jiban" ("My Life") was published in 1876. (आमार जीबन — राससुंदरी देवी)

• She taught herself to read and write secretly, at a time when literacy was forbidden to housewives in orthodox Bengali households.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sarala Devi Chaudhurani was a nationalist and the founder of the Bharat Stree Mahamandal (1910), the first all-India women's organisation; she was a niece of Rabindranath Tagore.

• Manikuntala Sen was a communist leader and author of the memoir "In Search of Freedom" (Shediner Kotha).

NOTE

• "Aamar Jiban" is a landmark text of 19th-century Bengal Renaissance literature and an important source on the social condition of women.

• Related firsts: Savitribai Phule — India's first woman teacher; Kadambini Ganguly and Anandibai Joshi — India's first women doctors.

question: Where is the Vivekanand Rock Memorial situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanyakumari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Vivekananda Rock Memorial stands on a small rocky island off the coast of Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu, where the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean meet. (विवेकानंद रॉक मेमोरियल — कन्याकुमारी)

• It was built in 1970 to mark the spot where Swami Vivekananda is believed to have meditated in 1892 and attained enlightenment before leaving for the World's Parliament of Religions, Chicago (1893).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The memorial was constructed largely through the efforts of Eknath Ranade and the Vivekananda Kendra.

• Nearby stands the 133-foot statue of the Tamil poet-saint Thiruvalluvar, author of the Thirukkural.

• Kanyakumari is the southernmost tip of mainland India.

NOTE

• Swami Vivekananda (1863–1902), born Narendranath Datta, was the chief disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897). His birthday, 12 January, is celebrated as National Youth Day.

question: Under which Act was the rule of British Crown established over India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government of India Act 1858.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Government of India Act, 1858 — also called the Act for the Good Government of India — abolished the East India Company and transferred the powers of government, territories and revenues directly to the British Crown. (भारत शासन अधिनियम 1858)

• It was passed in the wake of the Revolt of 1857.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Key features of the 1858 Act: it created the office of the Secretary of State for India (a member of the British Cabinet) assisted by a 15-member Council of India; it ended the Board of Control and the Court of Directors (i.e., the dual government of Pitt's India Act 1784); and the Governor-General was re-designated Viceroy of India — Lord Canning being the first Viceroy.

• Regulating Act of 1773 — the first step of British Parliamentary control; made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings).

• Charter Act of 1813 — ended the Company's trade monopoly in India (except in tea and trade with China).

• Charter Act of 1833 — made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (Lord William Bentinck) and centralised administration.

NOTE

• The proclamation of Queen Victoria at the Allahabad Durbar (1 November 1858), read by Lord Canning, announced the assumption of Crown rule. Victoria was later declared Empress of India by the Royal Titles Act, 1876.

question: The Kolar region of Karnataka is famous for which mineral from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gold.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kolar Gold Fields (KGF) in the Kolar district of Karnataka are famous for gold mining. (कोलार — सोना) For decades KGF was India's principal source of gold; the mines were finally closed in 2001.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other gold-bearing areas in India: Hatti (Raichur, Karnataka) — currently the only major working gold mine — and the Ramagiri fields (Anantapur, Andhra Pradesh).

• Coal: mainly from Jharkhand (Jharia, Bokaro), Odisha (Talcher), Chhattisgarh (Korba) and West Bengal (Raniganj).

• Petroleum: Mumbai High (offshore Maharashtra), Digboi (Assam), Ankleshwar (Gujarat).

• Copper: Khetri (Rajasthan), Singhbhum (Jharkhand), Balaghat (Madhya Pradesh).

NOTE

• Karnataka is India's leading producer of gold and is also rich in iron ore (Bellary–Hospet) and manganese. The KGF mines are among the deepest in the world.

question:
Match the following performances of Indian naatya, which were presented by the means of variegated components:

1) Angika          (a) costumes and make-up

2) Vachika        (b) depiction of mental or psychological states

3) Aharya          (c) spoken words

4) Sattvika       (d) gestures and other bodily movements
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1-d, 2-c, 3-a, 4-b.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni describes four kinds of abhinaya (modes of expression) used in Indian naatya (drama/dance):

◦ Angika abhinaya — expression through gestures and other bodily movements (अंगिक — शरीर की गति) → (d)

◦ Vachika abhinaya — expression through spoken words, song and recitation (वाचिक — वाणी) → (c)

◦ Aharya abhinaya — expression through costumes, make-up, ornaments and stage decor (आहार्य — वेशभूषा) → (a)

◦ Sattvika abhinaya — expression of mental or psychological states, the involuntary emotional response (सात्विक — मनोभाव) → (b)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Natya Shastra (c. 200 BCE – 200 CE) is the oldest surviving treatise on dramaturgy, dance and music, and is often called the fifth Veda (Panchama Veda).

• It expounds the Rasa theory — the eight/nine rasas (sentiments): Shringara, Hasya, Karuna, Raudra, Veera, Bhayanaka, Bibhatsa, Adbhuta and later Shanta.

NOTE

• All eight classical dance forms of India — Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya — draw upon the Natya Shastra's four abhinayas.

question: In Fencing, a contest between the two fencers is known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is bout.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In fencing, a bout is the term for a contest/match between two fencers. (तलवारबाज़ी — दो प्रतिद्वंद्वियों के बीच मुक़ाबला)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Riposte — an offensive action made immediately after successfully parrying the opponent's attack.

• Parry — a defensive action that deflects the opponent's blade away.

• Remise — a renewed attack made immediately after the first attack is parried, without withdrawing the arm.

• Other fencing terms: piste (the playing strip), en garde (the ready position), touch/touché (a valid hit), lunge, foible and forte.

NOTE

• Fencing has three weapons — foil, épée and sabre — and is one of the few sports that has featured in every modern Olympic Games since 1896.

• The international governing body is the Fédération Internationale d'Escrime (FIE).

question: In which year has the Government of India instituted Arjuna Award to recognise outstanding achievement in national sports events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1961.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Arjuna Award was instituted by the Government of India in 1961 to recognise outstanding achievement in national sports. (अर्जुन पुरस्कार — 1961)

• It is conferred by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and consists of a bronze statuette of Arjuna, a scroll of honour and a cash prize.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India's sports awards and the years they were instituted:

◦ Arjuna Award — 1961 (consistent outstanding performance over four years).

◦ Dronacharya Award — 1985 (outstanding coaches).

◦ Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award — 1991–92 (the highest sporting honour; earlier called the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna).

◦ Dhyan Chand Award — 2002 (lifetime achievement in sports).

◦ Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar — 2009 (for organisations promoting sports).

• The first Khel Ratna awardee was the chess Grandmaster Viswanathan Anand (1991–92).

NOTE

• National Sports Day is observed on 29 August, the birth anniversary of the hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand, and the sports awards are traditionally presented on this day.

question: ‘Atla Taddi’, a festival celebrated by married and unmarried women alike to seek the blessings of Devi Gauri for a long and happy married life and a suitable groom, respectively, is celebrated in ____________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Atla Taddi" (also written Atla Tadde) is a festival of Andhra Pradesh (and Telangana), observed by women who fast and worship Devi Gauri (Parvati). Married women pray for the long life of their husbands and a happy married life, while unmarried girls pray for a suitable groom. (अटला तद्दी — आंध्र प्रदेश)

• It falls on the third day after the full moon in the month of Ashwayuja (Ashwin), and "atlu" refers to the dosa-like pancakes offered to the goddess.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other major festivals of Andhra Pradesh: Ugadi (the Telugu New Year), Sankranti, Bathukamma (Telangana), Bonalu and the Tirupati Brahmotsavam.

• Similar women's fasting festivals elsewhere: Karva Chauth (North India), Vat Savitri (Maharashtra/UP), Teej (Rajasthan/Bihar) and Chhath (Bihar/Jharkhand/UP).

NOTE

• Andhra Pradesh's capital region is Amaravati; the state is famous for the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, Kuchipudi dance and the Kondapalli toys.

question: PT Usha was elected as the president of which association in December 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Olympic Association.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The legendary athlete P. T. Usha was elected President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) in December 2022. She is the first woman and the first Olympian to head the IOA. (भारतीय ओलंपिक संघ — पी. टी. उषा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pilavullakandi Thekkeparambil Usha, from Kerala, is nicknamed the "Payyoli Express" and the "Golden Girl of India".

• At the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics she missed a bronze in the 400 m hurdles by 1/100th of a second — the closest an Indian woman had come to an individual Olympic medal at that time.

• She won four golds and one silver at the 1986 Seoul Asian Games, and was honoured with the Padma Shri and the Arjuna Award. She was nominated to the Rajya Sabha in 2022.

NOTE

• The Indian Olympic Association, founded in 1927, selects and sends Indian teams to the Olympic Games, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games. Its first president was Sir Dorabji Tata.

question: According to the first Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021 report of NITI Aayog, which state stands at the first place in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to NITI Aayog's first National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report, released in November 2021, Bihar stood first — that is, it recorded the highest proportion of multidimensionally poor people (about 51.91% of its population) among all States and Union Territories. (बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2021 — बिहार शीर्ष पर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The order of the poorest States in that report was Bihar (51.91%) > Jharkhand (42.16%) > Uttar Pradesh (37.79%) > Madhya Pradesh (36.65%). Kerala (0.71%) was the least poor, followed by Goa, Sikkim and Tamil Nadu.

• India's national MPI is based on the global MPI of the UNDP and OPHI (Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative) and uses 12 indicators grouped under three dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living.

• Data source: the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-4, 2015-16) for the first report.

NOTE

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015. Its Chairperson is the Prime Minister, and it is headed operationally by a Vice-Chairperson and a CEO.

question: What is the full form of UPSC?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Union Public Service Commission.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• UPSC stands for the "Union Public Service Commission" — India's central recruiting agency, which conducts the Civil Services Examination and other all-India examinations. (संघ लोक सेवा आयोग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The UPSC is a constitutional body established under Articles 315 to 323 (Part XIV) of the Constitution of India.

• Its origins lie in the first Public Service Commission set up on 1 October 1926 under the Government of India Act, 1919; it became the Federal Public Service Commission under the Act of 1935 and the UPSC after independence.

• The Chairman and members are appointed by the President and hold office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

• Headquarters: Dholpur House, Shahjahan Road, New Delhi.

NOTE

• The UPSC conducts the Civil Services Exam (IAS/IPS/IFS), CDS, NDA, CAPF, Engineering Services, Combined Medical Services and the Indian Forest Service examinations. Recruitment for Group B and C posts is handled by the SSC (Staff Selection Commission).

question: To which of the state does Sattriya classical dance belong?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sattriya is the classical dance form of Assam. (सत्रीया — असम) It was introduced in the 15th–16th century by the great Vaishnava saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardeva as a medium of devotional expression (bhakti) in the monasteries called "sattras", from which the dance takes its name.

• Sattriya was formally recognised as a classical dance form by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The eight classical dances of India and their States:

◦ Bharatanatyam — Tamil Nadu

◦ Kathak — Uttar Pradesh

◦ Kathakali — Kerala

◦ Mohiniyattam — Kerala

◦ Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh

◦ Odissi — Odisha

◦ Manipuri — Manipur

◦ Sattriya — Assam

NOTE

• Sattriya is accompanied by the khol (drum), taal (cymbals) and flute, and performances draw on the Ankiya Naat plays of Sankardeva.

• Folk dances of Assam include Bihu, Bagurumba and Jhumur.

question: Who among the following was a renowned dancer and the first person from Odisha to receive ‘Padma Vibhushan’ in 2000?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra (1926–2004), the legendary Odissi dancer and guru, was the first person from Odisha to be awarded the Padma Vibhushan, which he received in 2000. (केलुचरण महापात्र — पद्म विभूषण, 2000)

• He is credited with reviving and codifying Odissi in the 20th century and giving it its present classical form.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He had earlier received the Padma Shri (1972) and the Padma Bhushan (1988), along with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and its Fellowship.

• His famous disciples include Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi, Madhavi Mudgal, Protima Bedi and Kumkum Mohanty.

• Gangadhar Pradhan and Mayadhar Raut were also distinguished Odissi gurus (Mayadhar Raut received the Padma Shri).

NOTE

• Order of civilian honours: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. They were instituted in 1954 and are announced on Republic Day.

• Odissi originated in the temples of Odisha and is associated with the Jagannath temple at Puri and the tradition of the Maharis and Gotipuas.

question: Which musical instrument does N Rajam play?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Violin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Prof. N. Rajam (Narmada Rajam) is a celebrated Indian violinist of the Hindustani classical tradition. (वायलिन वादिका — एन. राजम)

• She is famous for the "gayaki ang" style — playing the violin so that it imitates the human singing voice — a technique she learnt from Pandit Omkarnath Thakur.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She has been honoured with the Padma Shri (1984), the Padma Bhushan (2004), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and its Fellowship. She headed the Faculty of Performing Arts at Banaras Hindu University.

• Instrument–exponent pairs frequently asked in SSC:

◦ Sitar — Pandit Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan, Nikhil Banerjee

◦ Santoor — Pandit Shivkumar Sharma

◦ Sarod — Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, Ali Akbar Khan

◦ Shehnai — Ustad Bismillah Khan

◦ Flute (Bansuri) — Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia

◦ Tabla — Ustad Zakir Hussain, Alla Rakha

◦ Violin (Carnatic) — Dr. L. Subramaniam, Lalgudi Jayaraman

NOTE

• The violin is a bowed string (chordophone) instrument of Western origin that was adopted into both Carnatic and Hindustani music; it has four strings and is played with a bow.

question: Which of the following is NOT a function of money?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Barter system.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The barter system is not a function of money at all — it is the pre-monetary system of exchanging goods directly for goods, which money was invented to replace. (वस्तु विनिमय प्रणाली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The four main functions of money are:

◦ Medium of exchange — money is accepted in payment for goods and services, removing the need for a "double coincidence of wants".

◦ Unit of account (measure of value) — the value of every good is expressed in money terms.

◦ Store of value — purchasing power can be saved for future use.

◦ Standard of deferred payment — future payments (loans, salaries, rents) are stated in money.

• The main defects of the barter system were the lack of a double coincidence of wants, the absence of a common measure of value, the indivisibility of certain goods and the difficulty of storing wealth.

NOTE

• In India, currency notes are issued by the Reserve Bank of India (except the ₹1 note, issued by the Ministry of Finance), and coins are minted by the Government of India. Money supply measures are M1, M2, M3 and M4, with M3 as the "aggregate monetary resources".

question: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the population density recorded in Bihar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1106 persons/km².

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of India 2011, Bihar recorded a population density of 1,106 persons per square kilometre, making it the most densely populated State in India. (बिहार — 1106 व्यक्ति प्रति वर्ग किमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Population density = total population ÷ total land area.

• Census 2011 (15th Census) key figures:

◦ India's population — 121.09 crore; density — 382 persons/km².

◦ Most populous State — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim.

◦ Highest density among States — Bihar (1,106), followed by West Bengal (1,028) and Kerala (860); lowest — Arunachal Pradesh (17).

◦ Highest density among UTs — Delhi (11,320); overall sex ratio — 943; literacy rate — 74.04%.

◦ Motto of Census 2011 — "Our Census, Our Future".

NOTE

• The first complete synchronous census of India was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon; the first non-synchronous attempt was in 1872 under Lord Mayo. The census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948.

question: Carbohydrates are utilised by the human body in the form of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is glucose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All digestible carbohydrates (starch, sucrose, lactose, etc.) are broken down in the digestive tract into the simple sugar glucose, which is absorbed into the blood and used by the body's cells as their primary source of energy. (कार्बोहाइड्रेट — ग्लूकोज़ के रूप में)

• Glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) is oxidised during cellular respiration to release energy stored as ATP.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Amino acids are the digestion products of proteins, not carbohydrates.

• Nucleotides are the building blocks of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).

• Fibre (cellulose) is a carbohydrate that the human body cannot digest; it adds roughage and helps bowel movement.

• Excess glucose is stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles (and as fat).

NOTE

• Carbohydrates provide about 4 kcal per gram, proteins about 4 kcal/g, and fats about 9 kcal/g.

• Insulin (from the beta cells of the pancreas) lowers blood glucose, while glucagon raises it; their imbalance causes diabetes mellitus.

question: Which Indian musician is associated with the tabla?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Zakir Hussain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Zakir Hussain is the world-renowned Indian musician associated with the tabla. (तबला — ज़ाकिर हुसैन) He was the son and disciple of the great tabla maestro Ustad Alla Rakha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• He received the Padma Shri (1988), the Padma Bhushan (2002) and the Padma Vibhushan (2023), along with multiple Grammy Awards.

• He co-founded the fusion groups Shakti (with John McLaughlin) and Planet Drum (with Mickey Hart).

• Ustad Bismillah Khan — shehnai (Bharat Ratna, 2001).

• Pandit Ravi Shankar — sitar (Bharat Ratna, 1999).

• Ilaiyaraaja — a celebrated South Indian film composer.

NOTE

• The tabla is a pair of drums — the smaller wooden dayan/tabla played with the right hand and the larger metal bayan/dagga played with the left. It is a membranophone.

• Major tabla gharanas: Delhi, Ajrada, Lucknow, Farukhabad, Banaras and Punjab.

question: On whose advice did Gandhiji spend a year travelling around British India to know the people of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On returning from South Africa in January 1915, Mahatma Gandhi travelled across British India for one year on the advice of his political guru, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, in order to understand the country and its people before entering politics. (गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले — गांधीजी के राजनीतिक गुरु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Gopal Krishna Gokhale (1866–1915) was a moderate leader of the Indian National Congress, its President in 1905 (Banaras session), and the founder of the Servants of India Society (1905).

• Gandhiji called Gokhale his political guru and wrote about him in his autobiography "The Story of My Experiments with Truth".

• Shrimad Rajchandra, a Jain poet-philosopher, was Gandhiji's spiritual guide.

NOTE

• After this year of travel, Gandhiji founded the Satyagraha Ashram at Kochrab/Sabarmati (1915) and launched his first Indian satyagrahas at Champaran (1917), Ahmedabad (1918) and Kheda (1918).

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak called Gokhale the "Diamond of India"; Gandhiji's other mentors included Dadabhai Naoroji, the "Grand Old Man of India".

question: Which deficit indicates the borrowing requirements of the government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fiscal deficit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fiscal deficit is the excess of total government expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings. It therefore shows exactly how much the government needs to borrow in a financial year — that is, it indicates the borrowing requirement of the government. (राजकोषीय घाटा — सरकार की उधार आवश्यकता)

◦ Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure – Total Receipts (excluding borrowings)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure – Revenue Receipts. It shows that the government's current earnings fall short of its current spending.

• Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit – Interest Payments. It shows the current year's borrowing need excluding the burden of past debt.

• Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue Deficit – Grants for the creation of capital assets.

• "Capital deficit" is not a standard budgetary term.

NOTE

• The FRBM Act, 2003 (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act) sets targets for containing the fiscal deficit as a percentage of GDP.

• A high fiscal deficit can be financed by market borrowings, borrowing from the RBI (deficit financing) or disinvestment, and may lead to inflation and a debt trap.

question: Which of the following fundamental duties was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002?
option_1: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem
option_2: To protect and to improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures
option_3: To provide opportunities for education to his/her child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years
option_4: To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
solution_text:
The correct answer is To provide opportunities for education to his/her child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added the eleventh Fundamental Duty — Article 51A(k) — making it the duty of every parent or guardian "to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years". (86वां संविधान संशोधन, 2002)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The same 86th Amendment also:

◦ inserted Article 21A, making free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 a Fundamental Right, and

◦ modified Article 45 of the Directive Principles to cover early childhood care and education for children below six years.

• It led to the enactment of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

• The other three options are among the original ten Fundamental Duties added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, and are borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IV-A, Article 51A, of the Constitution and now number eleven. They are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts.

question: Which of the following rocks is formed during the metamorphism of rocks?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Slate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Slate is a metamorphic rock. It is formed when the sedimentary rock shale (or clay) is subjected to great heat and pressure deep within the Earth's crust. (स्लेट — कायांतरित चट्टान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Conglomerate and Sandstone are sedimentary rocks, formed by the compaction and cementation of gravel and sand respectively.

• Basalt is an extrusive igneous rock, formed by the rapid cooling of lava at the Earth's surface (the Deccan Traps are made of basalt).

• Important metamorphic transformations:

◦ Shale/Clay → Slate

◦ Limestone → Marble

◦ Sandstone → Quartzite

◦ Granite → Gneiss

◦ Coal → Graphite → Diamond

◦ Basalt → Schist

NOTE

• The three major rock types are igneous (formed from cooled magma/lava), sedimentary (formed from deposited sediments) and metamorphic (formed by heat and pressure acting on existing rocks). Their continuous transformation is called the rock cycle.

• Only sedimentary rocks normally contain fossils.
